methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $60M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Mitra Chem is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Vivas Kumar and Will Chueh that has raised $60M+ to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company operating in the same sector and stage cohort, including peers such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $60M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B to next-stage transitions, yielding $114M. The peer-median method references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals), generating a median implied value of $1.0B. These two methods produce a wide range reflecting the heterogeneity typical of pre-revenue or early-revenue climate-tech companies at this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $97M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $557M. The wide spread between methods reflects material uncertainty around near-term commercialization timelines, regulatory environment, and capital intensity—standard for frontier energy companies. The peer-median approach assumes Mitra Chem will achieve comparable scale and market position to Electric Hydrogen or similar cohort peers, while the stage-progression method grounds valuation more conservatively in observed capital deployment patterns.
